subtitle: An export interface study
description: A 12-inch drum layout explores a mill-duty envelope using the same modelling primitives. No AISE/AIST interchangeability, duty classification or compliance is asserted.
decisions: Keep a separate interface family instead of relabelling the DIN-oriented concept.
Buy actuation until the severe-duty force/time envelope is known.
Prioritize access for inspection and replacement in dirty environments.
materials: S355J2+N candidate structure with environment-specific coating.
Rotor and lining pair require mill-duty temperature and contamination assessment.
risks: All mounting dimensions are original placeholders, not an AIST drawing.
High cycle duty, hot surroundings and corrosion require a separate load spectrum.
steps: Obtain machine interface dimensions and applicable standard revision.
Review base, pivot and thruster positions against that interface.
Proceed with the drum-platform assembly sequence only after separate design approval.
validation: Interface metrology and full duty-cycle definition.
hypotheses: Timed inspection against the customer’s installed mill brake.
Measure actual reuse after duty loads are approved.
sensors: Advisory position / wear sensing with replaceable brackets; no AI-controlled brake release.
Record supplier sensor range, supply, connector, EMC, ingress and temperature limits before selection.
Define independent machine safety interface and diagnostic fault response with the responsible controls engineer.
